name: Run /files/search handlers off the API event loop
description:
Fix the event-loop blocking part of the chat `@` intellisense latency in api/codx/junior/api/files.py.

CURRENT PROBLEM: `@router.get("/files/search")` and `@router.get("/files/search-content")` are `async def` handlers that call the synchronous, CPU/disk-bound `file_engine.search_files(...)` / `file_engine.search_files_content(...)` directly. Because the work happens on the event loop thread, a multi-second search blocks every other request of the API (including the rest of the UI) on each keystroke.

WHAT TO IMPLEMENT (api/codx/junior/api/files.py only):
1. Keep the synchronous engine API as it is and call it through a worker thread: `import asyncio` and `return await asyncio.to_thread(file_engine.search_files, search=..., search_path=..., page=..., page_size=..., raw_search=..., use_regex=...)` (keyword arguments preserved). Do the same for `search_files_content`.
2. Copy the pattern already used in api/codx/junior/api/file_finder.py (`await asyncio.to_thread(file_manager.find_files, ...)`) - read that file for reference, do not modify it.
3. Keep the early-return short-circuits (`if not search:` / `if not query:`) BEFORE offloading, keep all query param parsing, defaults and response payloads identical, and do not touch any other endpoint in the file.
4. Update both docstrings to state that the search runs in a worker thread so large trees no longer block the event loop.

VERIFY BEFORE FINISHING: `cd api && python -m compileall codx/junior/api/files.py`, and `cd api && python -m pytest tests -q` (report pre-existing failures). Grep the file to confirm no remaining direct `file_engine.search_files(`/`search_files_content(` call outside `asyncio.to_thread`.

**Acceptance criteria**
Diff shows both handlers awaiting `asyncio.to_thread(...)` with unchanged parameters/response contracts and short-circuits kept before the offload; `python -m compileall codx/junior/api/files.py` is clean; no other endpoint in the module changed.

# ORCHESTRATED STEP
Run: **Fix chat intellisense latency on multi sub-project repos**
Step: **Run /files/search handlers off the API event loop** (`s2`)

## Run objective
Typing `@` in the chat composer is extremely slow (seconds to tens of seconds) when the active project has several sub-projects. Root cause analysis is already done and stored at .codx/profiles/orchestrator/knowledge/analysis/chat-intellisense-performance.md:

1. client/src/store/project.js `searchMentions` loops sequentially over [project, ...getRelatedProjects(project)] and each `searchProjectFiles` call AGAIN expands getRelatedProjects, producing O(N^2) sequential `GET /api/files/search` round-trips per keystroke. The backend already scopes the search to the current project root (which physically contains the sub-projects), so the client fan-out is pure duplication.
2. Backend `FileEngine.search_files` / `search_files_content` in api/codx/junior/engine/file_engine.py build a fresh `GitIgnoreManager` per call, whose `_load_all_gitignore_files` does a FULL os.walk, and then walk the tree a SECOND time for the search itself. With ~7k files per .worktrees tree one call takes seconds.
3. `GET /api/files/search` in api/codx/junior/api/files.py is an `async def` calling the blocking `file_engine.search_files`, so every keystroke blocks the whole API event loop.

Goal: make `@` mention intellisense feel instant (<300ms typical) on repositories with several sub-projects, without changing the public suggestion payload shape. Fix both the client fan-out and the backend full-tree re-walk / event-loop blocking, then verify with evidence (tests or a reproducible measurement, plus review of the diff).

## Step objective
Fix the event-loop blocking part of the chat `@` intellisense latency in api/codx/junior/api/files.py.

CURRENT PROBLEM: `@router.get("/files/search")` and `@router.get("/files/search-content")` are `async def` handlers that call the synchronous, CPU/disk-bound `file_engine.search_files(...)` / `file_engine.search_files_content(...)` directly. Because the work happens on the event loop thread, a multi-second search blocks every other request of the API (including the rest of the UI) on each keystroke.

WHAT TO IMPLEMENT (api/codx/junior/api/files.py only):
1. Keep the synchronous engine API as it is and call it through a worker thread: `import asyncio` and `return await asyncio.to_thread(file_engine.search_files, search=..., search_path=..., page=..., page_size=..., raw_search=..., use_regex=...)` (keyword arguments preserved). Do the same for `search_files_content`.
2. Copy the pattern already used in api/codx/junior/api/file_finder.py (`await asyncio.to_thread(file_manager.find_files, ...)`) - read that file for reference, do not modify it.
3. Keep the early-return short-circuits (`if not search:` / `if not query:`) BEFORE offloading, keep all query param parsing, defaults and response payloads identical, and do not touch any other endpoint in the file.
4. Update both docstrings to state that the search runs in a worker thread so large trees no longer block the event loop.

VERIFY BEFORE FINISHING: `cd api && python -m compileall codx/junior/api/files.py`, and `cd api && python -m pytest tests -q` (report pre-existing failures). Grep the file to confirm no remaining direct `file_engine.search_files(`/`search_files_content(` call outside `asyncio.to_thread`.

## Acceptance criteria
Diff shows both handlers awaiting `asyncio.to_thread(...)` with unchanged parameters/response contracts and short-circuits kept before the offload; `python -m compileall codx/junior/api/files.py` is clean; no other endpoint in the module changed.

## Known files
- `api/codx/junior/api/files.py`
- `api/codx/junior/api/file_finder.py`

## Rules
- Work only on this step; do not start unrelated refactors.
- Inspect the code before changing it and keep the change reviewable.
- Verify your work (tests, build, manual check) and say how.
- If you are blocked, explain exactly what is missing instead of guessing forever.

## Result contract
Finish with a JSON object (and nothing after it):
{"status":"done"|"blocked"|"failed","summary":"what was done","files":["paths touched"],"verification":"how you verified it","followups":["remaining work"]}
